title: How Much To Save for Home Furnishing & Setup Costs in the U.S.
description: Budgeting for the 'Empty Room' problem after buying a house.
content:
Buying a house is expensive, but filling it is the hidden budget killer. Many new homeowners spend their entire savings on the down payment, only to realize they have zero furniture for two of the three bedrooms. The cost of 'making a house a home'—from window treatments (blinds) to rugs and sofas—can easily run 10-15% of the home's purchase price over the first year. This guide helps you calculate a realistic 'Furnishing Sinking Fund' so you don't end up sleeping on a mattress on the floor.

Key Takeaways

  • The 10-25% Rule: Interior designers estimate furnishing a home costs 10% (budget) to 25% (luxury) of the home's value. On a $400k home, budget $40k over time.
  • Window Treatment Shock: Blinds and curtains are surprisingly expensive. Budget $200-$500 per window for custom fit, or $50/window for DIY IKEA solutions.
  • The 'Room by Room' Strategy: Don't furnish the whole house at once. Furnish the Master Bedroom and Living Room (Phase 1). Leave the Guest Room empty until you have cash (Phase 2).
  • Second-Hand Value: Hard furniture (tables/dressers) should be bought used (Facebook Marketplace) to save 70%. Soft furniture (mattresses/sofas) is often worth buying new for hygiene.

Why It Matters (US Context)

Supply chain delays often mean new furniture takes 3-6 months to arrive. Buying 'In Stock' items or high-quality used items allows you to settle in immediately without financing a $5,000 couch on a store credit card.

The 'New House' Bill of Materials

Estimates for a 2,000 sq ft home.

Phase 1: Essentials (Day 1)

  • Mattress & Frame: $1,500.
  • Sofa: $1,500.
  • Dining Table/Chairs: $800.
  • Kitchen Basics (Pots/Plates): $500.
  • Shower Curtains/Towels: $200.
  • Total: $4,500 (Cash needed before moving).

Phase 2: Privacy & Comfort (Month 1-3)

  • Blinds/Shades: $1,500 (DIY) to $5,000 (Professional).
  • Rugs: $1,000 ($300 each x 3 rooms).
  • Lighting: $500.
  • Total: ~$3,000.

Phase 3: The 'Nice to Haves' (Year 1)

Guest bed, Patio furniture, Art, Bookshelves.
Budget: $5,000 - $10,000.

How to Save for It

  1. The 'Closing Cost' Overflow: When saving for the house, add $5,000 to your target specifically for Phase 1. Do not use this for the down payment.
  2. Housewarming Registry: Create an Amazon registry for your housewarming party. Put practical items (tools, kitchenware) on it. Friends want to help.
  3. 0% Financing (Caution): Furniture stores offer 0% for 24 months. Only use this if you have the cash sitting in a HYSA earning 5% interest. Pay it off one month early.
  4. Estate Sales: The best way to get high-quality solid wood furniture for cheap. Go on the last day of the sale for 50% off.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I rent furniture?

No. Rent-to-Own centers charge 200%+ effective interest. You pay $3,000 for a $500 couch. Sleep on an air mattress before renting furniture.

Is IKEA worth it?

For starters, yes. But particle board doesn't move well. If you plan to move again soon, IKEA might break. Solid wood used furniture lasts longer.

What is the most important purchase?

The Mattress. You spend 1/3 of your life there. Don't cheap out on sleep quality. Save $1,500 for a good one.
